text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000116 bills 99215 well above risk-adjusted expectation, including at the lowest complexity tiers, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share appears in every complexity tier, not just among sicker patients, and over a third of 99215s go to patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. The sampled low-complexity 99215s include visits for codes such as rash (R21), unspecified abdominal pain (R10.9), low back pain (M54.50) and follow-up (Z09), for example C0067807, C0067799, C0067821 and C0068249, which is a pattern consistent with upcoding. Against that, the panel is also skewed toward 99214, and the few charts returned do not point toward upcoding: all three documented 99215s (C0068133, C0068167, C0068654) support the billed level. Only one 99214 (C0068459) was documented below the billed level, and no notes claiming substantial data review lacked a lab or test line. Still, the 18 documented claims are too few to judge. A reviewer should first request charts specifically for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed, especially the symptom-only and Z09 visits, and check whether MDM and time support level 5."}
